newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to issue T-bills on September 10.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to issue T-bills on September 10.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank will auction three-month, six-month, nine-month and 12-month discount treasury bills on September 10, a central bank official said on Monday.

The central bank is setting the denominations of T-bills at 100 hryvnia and is not setting the issue volume in advance, the head of the bank's capital markets and exchange department, Vitaly Migashko, told Reuters.

At the last auction of three-month discount T-bills on September 4, the bank sold 6.399 million hryvnia worth of paper, with an average annualised yield of 57.25 percent. The average price was 87.51 hryvnia.

At the last auction of six-month discount T-bills on September 5, the bank sold 34.194 million hryvnia worth of paper, with an average annualised yield of 62.29 percent. The average price was 76.30 hryvnia.
The last auctions of nine-month and 12-month discount T-bills took place before introduction of new Ukraine's currency, the hryvnia.
One hryvnia equals 100,000 karbovanets, the old currency.

At the last auction of nine-month discount T-bills on August 20, the bank sold 770 million karbovanets worth of paper, with an average annualised yield of 56.21 percent. The average price was 7.040 million karbovanets.

At the last auction of 12-month discount T-bills on August 16, the bank sold 4.695 trillion karbovanets worth of paper, with an average annualised yield of 56.65 percent. The average price was 6.390 million karbovanets.
